decisions.reason: Although it has not been visible on the website recently, an encrypted second channel remains central to the firm's core authentication and secure communication platform, so management would usually retain it unless it is fully absorbed into a broader offer.

Mobile PDF signing still fits the firm's direction toward app-based interactions and digital contracting, but as a narrower function with no recent visibility it faces a moderate risk of being folded into a larger signing workflow rather than continued as a distinct product.

A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is strategically close to the firm's cryptography-driven identity platform, so a medium-sized German security specialist would normally continue it despite possible rebranding or bundling.

A QR-code-based hardware token is comparatively less aligned with the firm's move toward software-centric, cross-channel mobile identity solutions and is the most plausible candidate for withdrawal after several years without visible market presence.

Payment-security compliance remains attractive for regulated enterprise customers and fits the firm's security infrastructure strengths, though the lack of recent website evidence raises a meaningful chance of consolidation into broader compliance or authentication offerings.
